content.title: My Surface Laptop Studio Review

Skip to main content Surface Laptop Studio sitting on my sofa Note: Everything reported here are my personal thoughts based on the way I use this device. This means it does not represent Microsoft in any statement and also you can have different opinion based on your own way of working. The Long Story... I was able to get the new Surface Laptop Studio just one day before the official launch in Switzerland. I was waiting for this device to be available since the announcement in September last year and I'm really excited to have in my hand! I'm coming from a long path and experience with Surface line-up. My first device was the Surface Pro (1), then I got the Surface Pro 2, Book 1, Book 2, Laptop 3 and, just before this, I had a Surface Book 3 as main device. I still have a Surface Pro X as on-the-road device. The way I use the device is quite particular: I use it for my regular work (documents, meetings, whiteboard, coding) but also for my hobbies including photo & video editing and drawing. For these reasons a convertible laptop is essential to me: something that can move from regular laptop to a tablet with the best drawing feedback is possible. Also, when I'm working at home, I 3D-printed a stand so that I can use external keyboard and mouse for a better experience. Surface Book 3 was actually a really good companion for long sessions of work and fun, with one big issue: cooling. The Surface Book 3 CPU and GPU (13.5inch) in the screen is passively cooled "fanless" but in the position I was using it, the air flow is stopped by the keyboard attached behind the screen making it really hot and slowing down the CPU speed to avoid damage. This was saving the laptop but making the surface unusable for the tasks I was doing. The Surface Laptop Studio is, instead, actively cooled (with 2 fans - one for the CPU and one for the GPU). This was one of the reasons I decided to go with for it and give a try. Now let's give a look of what I found good, bad and ugly using this new baby on the field! The Good let's start from the good we have.. and it's a lot! The build quality. The Surface Laptop Studio is the best Surface device ever build (full stop). The quality of the material is extremely high and comparable with any other super high-end device in the market (you know what I'm talking about right?😏). Even the screen flipping mechanics is extremely reliable and build to last (and this was one of my doubt). The way it flips. Compared with my Surface Book 3 the way the Surface Laptop flips it's for me an advantage. Not relaying on software to detach the additional battery and the GPU it's a super plus! I will miss the Power button on the top anyway now that its integrate in the keyboard. Recommended by LinkedIn Microsoft releases a new Laptop to the Surface Family… Sophia Sark-Geissler 8 years ago PixelSense™: Only on Microsoft Surface The Laptop Company Limited 1 year ago A Pro-iPad: A world of possibilities Rajarshi Rakesh S. 10 years ago The 14.4inch screen. It is gorgeous: Sharp, colorful and bright with the bonus of that 120Hz refresh rate, something you don't expect from a laptop not specifically designed for gaming. The keyboard and the touchpad. This is one of the most enjoyable keyboard to use for writing and even better that many external ones. One thing I really don't like is that the power button so close to the Delete and Backspace keys but this is something inherited from the Surface Laptop so not really a new thing. Just below you have the Precision Haptics touchpad. it uses special haptic engines to send a vibration to your finger when it feels extra pressure and it's in my opinion even better than all the other high-end super laptop in the market ;) The audio. Just Wow... Here we have the quad Omnisonic speakers turning every sound in a concert: 4 speakers - two woofers on the sides and two tweeners pushing sound through the keyboard. Thunderbolt (finally). The Surface Laptop Studio has only three ports and a headphone jack. One is the "classic" Surface Connect port, but (Hallelujah!) the last two are two Thunderbolt 4 (USB4) ports: This means better docking stations and external graphic cards can finally be connected to this device. Battery Life. Better than the SB3 for sure and more than ok-ish for a i7 CPU.. At the end is not an ARM architecture if you do comparison.. ;) The Bad All the roses comes with thorns right? and I know you were waiting for this :) Again, these are all my opinions and maybe are not relevant for you.. So always compare with your needs! CPU and GPU combination. The Surface Laptop Studio is coming at high-end with a Intel Core i7-11370H CPU (Tiger Lake) with 4 cores (8 threads - 35W/28W TDP). I was expecting some more like Core i7-11800H with 8 cores (16 threads - 45W/35W TDP) as this one will not impact the battery life so much and give a lot more power to play with. Same story for the GPU the RTX 3050Ti (4GB) where the RTX 3060 (6GB) could be more appropriate here with a big jump in terms of performance. Don't take me wrong, the Surface Laptop Studio is the fastest Surface ever build.. but if you are looking for a top-performer for gaming or content creation... well.. you are not exactly in the right place. PCIe Lines. With Tiger Lake's 4 PCIe 4.0 lanes tied up driving the RTX 3050Ti to squeeze out whatever is possible from it, Microsoft has instead hung their SSD off of the PCIe lanes coming from the PCH. This in turn means that the storage options are limited to PCIe 3.0 reducing the benefit of the read/write speed you can get from the latest PCIe 4.0 SSD drives. It's also true that the latest PCIe 4.0 SSD are intensive power-eater.. So again for a battery life prospective this is better but it's compromising the performance. Removable solid-state drive. Theoretically, you can replace the SSD coming in the Surface Laptop studio. But as pointed out in the website this should be done only by skilled technician following Microsoft provided instructions. The reason is that is really difficult to open the Surface Laptop Studio so I would not recommend that to anyone. Card Reader. What I loved of my Surface Book 3 and I will miss a lot as photographer is the integrated card reader. The idea to not relay on an external device to read my camera cards was always a plus for me. It's bad this was removed in the Surface Laptop Studio. The Ugly Apart from the previous paragraph where I highlighted some of technical gaps I found, there are some aesthetics and design decision I don't really like/agree with. Again... this is all personal and maybe are not relevant or even a plus for you. The back shape. If you look at the Surface Laptop Studio from the top, it's amazing and strictly adheres to Microsoft's utilitarian design language (and also really close to the other super high-end device in the market..😏) but if you turn it upside, the slab stuck to the bottom it's not that "elegant" even if it's used to store and recharge the Slim Pen 2. Anyway I understand the reason for it: you have the battery packs and the active cooling system in there (2 fans, with separate cooling circuits for GPU and CPU). So sacrifice a bit of good-looking for a better cooling system is something I was looking for coming from the Surface Book 3 experience. But this bring us also to the next point. The hot air on your hand. the design of the cooling system pushes hot air out from the laptop on both sides of the laptop far away from the screen. the problem is that the hottest points are exactly where are your hands when are you typing on the keyboard and where you usually have your external mouse. it's not something that will burn you.. but anyway it's a particular design choice I will say.. The rounded monitor corners. The monitor is stunning as already said, but the rounded frame containing it is a bit less "nice". The pointer completely disappears when pushed as far as possible on the corner. Not a big deal again.. but anyway something to notice. The Final Verdict (for me!) So, we are now coming finally to the end. How is the Surface Laptop Studio for what I do? Am I happy? Compared with my Surface Book 3 (i7/32GB/GTX 1650 - 2 years old) I got more power, a better battery life, a better screen and a super nice "flipping" experience and I removed one of my pain point: cooling issues. So YES. It worth any euro/dollar/swiss franc I paid for it - and they are quite a lot as it's a premium laptop. But the other super high-end devices in the market are not cheap neither and they have limitation as well. Looking at it more in general, in my opinion this is a extremely good productivity laptop build with the vision of maximizing user experience without excelling in any specific vertical: The processor is indeed a really good processor, the external GPU is present and decent, the trio screen/keyboard/touchpad is the best in class you can get on the market and most of the weaknesses are coming from the intent to extend the battery life as much as possible. Of course, if you are looking for a gaming laptop or a content creation laptop you have more specialized devices in the market that are rocking there. But if you want something more-than-good-enough in many areas, I really recommend you to have a look the Surface Laptop Studio.
